source_text_span: Lesions start as water-soaked, yellow-orange stripes on leaf tips or margins with wavy edges.
Cut a leaf section with lesions and place in clear water; cloudy bacterial ooze streams out into the water.
Bacterial leaf blight is favored by high relative humidity, rainstorms, and stagnant standing water in paddies.
Nitrogen deficiency causes general yellowing starting strictly on the lowest, oldest leaves as nitrogen is remobilized.
Nitrogen deficiency typically affects large areas or entire fields uniformly due to low soil nitrogen status.
Water deficit causes inward longitudinal leaf rolling and folding into tube-like shapes to reduce transpiration.
Leaf rolling and wilting due to water stress is reversed within 24 hours following rainfall or field irrigation.
Blast lesions on leaves are typically diamond-shaped or elliptical with gray or whitish centers and reddish-brown to dark brown margins.
Neck blast attacks the panicle base node turning it grayish-brown or black and causing it to rot and snap, producing empty whiteheads.
Blast is favored by long periods of free moisture on leaves from dew, overcast skies, and high nitrogen fertilizer levels.
Brown spot produces small, circular to oval dark brown spots resembling sesame seeds, typically with a light yellow halo.
Brown spot severity is closely correlated with poor, nutrient-deficient soils, particularly those lacking potassium, iron, or silicon.
